pairs.why: Both are near-identical soft-clay campfires; B's logs have slightly clearer cut ends and a tidier stone ring, so it reads a little more like a built object.
A's logs show distinct cut ends and wood grain, closer to the moderately textured real wood; B is a bit softer and more generic.
B's teepee of logs with visible end rings is more convincingly constructed than A's glowing, rubbery logs.
A's logs have readable cut ends and slightly more surface detail, matching the real cards' light-but-present texture better than B's smoother logs.
A's logs keep a brown wood color with defined ends, like the real stew-pot logs, while B's logs glow orange all over and look more like plastic.
Nearly a tie; B's logs and flame are slightly better defined, but it's a marginal call.
A's darker, grained logs with glowing cut ends read more like real wood in the game's moderately smooth finish; B is smoother and more toy-like.
A's logs have clearer structure and end grain, and its stones sit more naturally, which matches the real cards' finish slightly better than B.
